self.created = True
        try:
            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as handle:
                handle.write(self.token)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
evidence.reason: The acquire path creates the marker with O_CREAT|O_EXCL, records created=True, then fsyncs only the token file descriptor; it never fsyncs the parent directory. The code's own comments and recovery handling show persistence across failure is intended, so losing the directory entry on power failure defeats the admission hold. The finding's release-side point (line 459) is the same omission: an unsynced unlink can resurrect a stale hold after reboot, permanently refusing admission until manual recovery. This is an ordinary crash-consistency defect in existing intended behavior, not a new requirement; the smallest fix is to fsync the parent directory after creation and after removal and surface sync failure as an unverified admission transition.
